verdicts.rationale: The burst has no authored buff/heal/shred effect (effects: []), so there is no rendered window to diverge from. Every component of Wolf Within is constitution-excluded: added Electro DMG alongside normals (damage numbers), ATK SPD (attack-speed), Electro RES + Electro-Charged immunity + interruption resistance (defensive), the charged-attack disable (Razor's CA is not modeled anyway), and the on-swap energy return (energy). Nothing decision-relevant to buff/heal/cooldown expectations is silently omitted, and there is no wired primitive that could model a decision-relevant effect here (attack-speed and damage are out of scope), so implement does not apply. A Razor player already knows the burst is a personal steroid that ends on swap.
rubricRefs: noCaveat: no rendered surface to diverge from; constitution-excluded contents

groundedIn.claim: Wolf Within's benefits are added Electro DMG on normals, ATK SPD and Electro RES, Electro-Charged immunity, a charged-attack disable, and interruption resistance — all constitution-excluded categories
groundedIn.quote:
·Strikes alongside Razor's normal attacks, dealing Electro DMG.
·Raises Razor's ATK SPD and Electro RES.
·Causes Razor to be immune to DMG inflicted by the Electro-Charged status.
·Disables Razor's Charged Attacks.
·Increases Razor's resistance to interruption.

groundedIn.claim: The 15s status is a self-status with no authored effect and no spawned entity, so no window renders
groundedIn.quote: Wolf Within is a 15-second self-status on Razor … terminated when Razor swaps off-field (event.OnCharacterSwap). Not a spawned entity — not modeled as summons[]. `duration` field removed from ability per recipe.

groundedIn.claim: A Razor player already knows these effects end on swap (core kit knowledge)
groundedIn.quote: These effects end when Razor leaves the battlefield.

verdicts.rationale: C2 is authored as a self CRIT Rate buff gated on enemyHpBelow: 30, which the planner cannot simulate, so it renders optimistically (always-on). This is the canonical enemyHpBelow optimistic-render case: the CAN list marks these as 'render assumed-true + caveat', and the guide's Diluc C1 example names Razor C2 directly as the same treatment. The timeline shows the +10% CRIT Rate as always active when in game it applies only against opponents below 30% HP — a real, decision-relevant divergence that is un-implementable because enemy HP is not simulable. A player would be misled into treating the CRIT Rate as permanent rather than execute-range only. [Adjudicated per waves-3/4 verifier REJECT: passive-trigger constellation buffs render on no surface (buffWindows dispatch verified), so nothing misleads; the cited style-guide example was fabricated. Recorded in the renderer-follow-up class sweep.]
